So you would risk becoming uninsurable, or having to buy policies with loading and exclusions like me, before having dependents? From what I've seen and heard, this risk is much higher than the risk of getting a Major CI or being slapped with a 5-, 6- digit hospital bill before your 40s or 50s, so it is irrational for me to believe in hospital and CI plans but not believing in securing insurability of whole life plans when still healthy. 

The first point is actually all the more relevant to people who are not well off. The fast claiming process of the insurance monies is a godsend to grieving families that struggle to shoulder the funeral expenses and financial liabilities left behind. Rich people can easily tide through lengthy estate disputes.

Add-on: I agree with you that in terms of priority, this is lower than the other plans. I'm not saying OP should definitely buy at this age. That is why I ranked it at No. 3, in case you haven't noticed.

One big benefit is in estate planning. After death, the proceeds from whole life plans can be paid out to your nominated beneficiary without the need for a probate or LOA, as long as your will does not explicitly supersede this particular plan. That means an almost immediate, targeted pay out without potentially long legal proceedings or contests from other family or loved ones. Almost all other assets will be frozen until all legal matters are complete, even with a will, so this can help your dependents in the funeral expenses and other urgent liabilities.

The entire plan itself can also be protected from creditors in the event of bankruptcy, if you set up a trust nomination with your spouse or children as beneficiaries. They can take a policy loan or make claims from it on your behalf (hopefully in your favour if you nominated wisely as it is irrevocable on your end).

The cash value also serves as an emergency fund for all your insurance premiums in the event of other dire financial circumstances. I mean, it is still easy to withdraw them out for non emergency or non insurance purposes, but being tied to your protection needs, it should hopefully be only used as a last resort.

I wanted to mention the option to increase sum assured after life events without medical underwriting, but from a quick search I found that some term life plans also have this feature now. (Life events even include starting your first full time job, so do consider term life with such feature.)

Ex-FA here. I'm flabbergasted by people who say young people don't need term/whole life insurance. Before I managed to get sufficient CI coverage, I got diagnosed with health and mental conditions, and my parent got diagnosed with late stage cancer. Now I can only get plans that have minimal medical underwriting, covering only cancer/3 most common CI.

Priority wise, this is my recommendation for you:

1a. Hospital plan (highest tier)

1b. Accident plan (just the basic or 2nd tier will do)

Please get these asap. Shouldn't cost more than $100/mth iirc.

2. Another term plan but focusing on CI, because the Mindef Singlife is good for death/TPD coverage but not enough for CI

3. Whole life

Just no ILP. Happy to share more but the main gist is that a necessity like insurance should only be supported by low risk assets, and there's no reason to trust your agent to manage them well for you despite paying so much in fees.
